subject: Redwood Private VPC - post-demo summary & next tests
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>, Bob Liu <bob.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood Private VPC - post-demo summary & next tests

Hi Alice & Bob,

Thanks again for the time today - appreciate the deep dive into Acme Health's constrained networking requirements. Quick recap and the set of pragmatic next tests we agreed on: 

- Recap of what we showed: Redwood Private (VPC) with optional air-gapped control plane, configurable KMS integrations, and per-tenant network policies. We demoed an isolated deployment and walked through the control-plane UI and perf profiles.

- Key Acme asks / risks:
  - Strict egress restrictions from compute nodes; potential requirement for fully air-gapped inference with an on-prem control plane.
  - Integration with your existing VPN/IPSec termination.
  - Deterministic latency needs for batch inference vs streaming; cost targets for 99th percentile.

- Next tests (proposed):
  1) Networking punchlist: validate outbound-only rules and test NAT/proxy flow (we'll provide a checklist).
  2) Control-plane isolation: deploy a private control plane in your VPC + validate no outbound to Redwood public endpoints.
  3) Air-gap feasibility: one small on-prem sandbox where we attempt a fully isolated install (no internet except for signed artifact transfer).
  4) Competitor comparison notes: we will provide a short matrix vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints (networking controls, control plane residency, tooling for rollouts).

Attached is the initial networking checklist (high level) - Camila from infra will pick up the deep networking tests.

Can you confirm owners for the three tests and preferred dates next week? If you want, we can stand up a k8s sandbox for the control-plane test on Monday/Tuesday.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-networking-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

> Hi Alice & Bob,
>
> Thanks again for the time today - appreciate the deep dive into Acme Health's constrained networking requirements. Quick recap and the set of pragmatic next tests we agreed on: ...

Camila here (infra/solutions):

High-level asks from our side to run the tests reliably:
- A non-production VPC with a pair of subnets (private) where we can provision a control-plane EC2 or k8s nodes.
- NAT/proxy config (IP ranges) for the nodes that may need limited egress for image pulls. For air-gapped test we will provide signed artifacts to your ops team.
- A test service account with access to your internal VPN termination and a point-of-contact who can approve temporary firewall rules.

I'll prepare a more detailed network checklist and a short config snippet for iptables/proxy we recommend. Attaching a sample config we often use for the control-plane isolation test.

--
Camila Reyes
Infra Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Camila,

Thanks for the clear recap. Two quick clarifications from Acme ops and architecture before we lock dates: 

1) Competitor comparison: can you send a one-page matrix versus the major hyperscalers (AWS SageMaker endpoints / GCP/Vertex AI / Azure ML) that focuses specifically on networking and control-plane residency? Our security team is primarily concerned about where control-plane metadata lives and whether any telemetry is sent outside the VPC.

2) Air-gap feasibility: how long does the signed-artifact transfer + install typically take on our side? We're trying to scope a maintenance window. Also curious about rollback/upgrade paths if we go air-gapped.

Owners: I'll coordinate with Bob (infra lead) on firewall approvals. We can tentatively target Tue Nov 30 for control-plane isolation if Redwood can provide the sandbox steps and artifacts by Friday.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Director of IT Architecture | Acme Health
alice.chen@acmehealth.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>, Bob Liu <bob.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood Private VPC - post-demo summary & next tests

Alice - great questions. Short answers and proposed plan: 

1) Competitor matrix: we'll send a concise 1-pager that contrasts networking controls, control-plane residency (managed vs customer-owned), artifact distribution options for air-gapped installs, and what telemetry (if any) is transmitted by default. Expect this by EOD Thursday. We'll explicitly call out differences vs AWS/GCP/Azure managed endpoints (most hyperscalers keep control-plane metadata in their cloud).

2) Air-gap install timeline: for a small sandbox we typically do: artifact handoff (signed tarball) + ops install (2-4 hours) + verification (1-2 hours). For full production installs it's longer (planned maintenance window + rollback checklist). We'll include rollback/upgrade notes in the tech doc.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu Nov 26 - Redwood sends: (a) competitor matrix, (b) detailed networking checklist, (c) signed artifact + install instructions.
- Tue Nov 30 - Control-plane isolation test (tentative) - Acme to open temporary firewall/NAT for the sandbox subnets.

Can you confirm Bob as the point of contact for firewall approvals? Once confirmed we'll log the test in HubSpot and share a short runbook.

Links & docs: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACMEHEALTH (we'll attach the matrix and runbook there)

Thanks - looking forward to the tests.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
